assumptions: That the feature flag was the trigger is inferred from timing and log correlation only — the flag was never verifiably turned off, so the causal link was never demonstrated by removing it.

The remediation attempt is assumed to have failed to apply rather than to have applied and been ineffective: the action was logged with an empty target ('revert-feature-flag on None'), the flag continued to log as 'on', and the change record shows it being switched on again at 15:24:49. The actual behaviour of the flag-provider integration was not verified.

The divide-by-zero is assumed to be a pre-existing defect made reachable by the flag rather than newly shipped code. This rests on the absence of a deploy record for io-shop; no source or release inspection was performed.

Impact is assumed to be limited to account-page requests, based solely on service log lines. No user-facing or business telemetry was consulted, and no check was made for downstream effects on other services or on customers who abandoned the page.
The background UpstreamTimeout errors present before 15:16 are assumed to be unrelated pre-existing noise, not a contributing factor.

The incident end timestamp reflects escalation to humans, not confirmed recovery; errors were still being logged at that point. The duration therefore measures the automation's involvement, not the customer-visible outage.
The exact condition that produces the division by zero (which accounts, which data shape) was not identified; it is assumed to affect a subset of accounts, since not all requests failed.
input.executive_summary: For roughly ten minutes on the afternoon of 16 September, a large share of customers who opened their account page on the shop got an error instead of the page. Ordering and the rest of the site were not implicated; the failures were confined to the account page. The cause was a newly switched-on feature — a monthly spending summary — whose calculation failed for many customers as soon as it was turned on. The automated responder detected the problem within a minute, identified the newly enabled feature as the cause, and attempted to switch it back off. That attempt did not take hold: the feature continued to run and customers continued to see errors, and the responder, seeing no improvement, discarded its own (correct) explanation and went back to investigating. After two further rounds of investigation it handed the incident to on-call engineers. Customer-facing errors were still occurring at the moment of handover; nothing in this record confirms that service was restored, so the recovery and any customer communication sit with the human responders, not with the automation.
input.root_cause: At 15:16 UTC the feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` began evaluating "on" for io-shop (a partial rollout in that first minute, fully "on" thereafter), and the code path it enables raised `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32 while rendering account pages; every error line from 15:16 onward names that exception, whereas the preceding hour shows only sparse, unrelated `UpstreamTimeout` errors while the flag read "off". The underlying divide-by-zero is a latent defect in already-deployed code (no deploy appears in the change record for the service before the incident) that only became reachable when the flag was turned on. This attribution is strong but was never confirmed by experiment: the automated flag revert at 15:21:43 was recorded against no target, the flag continued to log as "on" through 15:25, and the change record shows `monthly-spend-feature` being switched ON again at 15:24:49 — so the hypothesis was marked "refuted" on the basis of a remediation that, on the available evidence, never actually took effect.
